messages:
Maya: Quick async standup — kernel/batching/KV perf smoke. TL;DR: canary landed, benched, saw p99 tail spike on long seqs.

Maya: What I did: landed microbatch refactor on canary (PR #2345), added a passive slotting metric, ran 30m load vs model:m72 on the canary pool.

Maya: Bench highlights (local run):
```
bench: 30m steady traffic
p50 14ms, p95 48ms, p99 310ms
throughput 125 req/s
kv_hit_rate 84% (prefix cache)
ooms: 0
```

Igor: Nice. Did you enable the new eviction window?

Maya: Yes — eviction window=20s for this canary. I suspected eviction thrash so I bumped it from 8s -> 20s. Helps kv_hit slightly but p99 still bad for sequences >1024.

Alex: @Maya can you paste the kernel logs around a p99 trace? want to see if it's microbatch coalescing causing head-of-line.

Maya: Pasted snippet below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-10T15:12:04Z] slot_alloc id=0x7fb start_seq=1 len=1200 wait_for_batch_ms=88
[2026-03-10T15:12:04Z] batch_emit id=0x7fb microbatch_size=4 kv_prefetch_hit=true
[2026-03-10T15:12:04Z] kernel_execute id=0x7fb tok=1024 exec_ms=204
```

Liam: That wait_for_batch_ms=88 seems high. Which batching policy on that shard?

Maya: policy=adaptive-latency, max_batch=8, dynamic_slotting=true. I think for long sequences adaptive waits too long trying to fill batches, which increases end-to-end p99 when a single long seq blocks a slot.

Sam: Could be slot stealing interaction with KV prefetch. If prefetch is serial and a long seq triggers a big KV miss path, it can block the microbatch. We saw similar in q4 tests.

Igor: Action items: 1) @Maya roll microbatch refactor back to max_batch=4 in canary to confirm hypothesis; 2) @Alex add per-request timeline traces (slot allocate -> kv prefetch -> kernel start) to the debug traces; 3) @Liam run a narrow replay with synthetic long sequences to reproduce.

Maya: Ack. I'll flip max_batch to 4 and restart canary. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary/m72-microbatch-refactor @ 5140009888 — health checks running.

Maya: After flip (10m run): p95 46ms, p99 128ms, throughput ~118 req/s, kv_hit 85%. Much better but still gap for very long tails.

Alex: Good signal. If traces confirm microbatch wait is the main factor we can tune the adaptive threshold to avoid waiting for batch fill when sequence length > 512.

Liam: I'll queue a replay with 2k-length synthetic requests across 3 shards and capture slot wait histograms. ETA ~2h.

Sam: Also let's check GC/allocator metrics on those hosts — long kernel exec + GC pause could explain weird p99s. pinging @Igor to add the allocator counters to the canary dashboards.

Igor: Will add allocator.free_ms and minor_gc_count to the canary panel.

Maya: Blockers: need a quick code review on the microbatch rollback config change (tiny diff). @Alex mind a quick approve? PR #2348 — it's a one-line change to max_batch default.

Alex: On it, will review in 10.

Maya: Today plan: finish traces, confirm whether prefetch or batch waiting causes tail; if it's prefetch, prototype parallel prefetch for KV on the hot path; if it's batch waiting, tune adaptive threshold and rerun 1h smoke.

Liam: FYI I saw a minor slot leak earlier on one host — created issue #523. Might be related; I'll attach heap dump.

Maya: Thanks — that could explain rare slot stalls.

Alex: Reviewed PR #2348 — approved, leaving a nit. @Maya you can merge when CI passes. :thumbsup:

Maya: Merged after CI green. Deploy-bot: canary updated at 5140009910.

deploy-bot: canary deploy successful: canary/m72-microbatch-refactor @ 5140009910 — all checks OK.

Sam: Follow-up: let's add a short eval job that submits a mix of short/long sequences to the canary hourly so we catch regressions quickly. I can wire that in Optimize.

Maya: Sounds good. Thanks all — I'll post the trace links and bench artifacts once uploads finish (should be <30m). :eyes:
